overview: A one-page Department of State filing list for decimal file 894.65, recording two papers concerning Japanese industry in 1936. The first is Tokyo telegram no. 1225, associated with Garrels, about proposed Japanese legislation to prevent disclosure of commercial information concerning Japanese factories and cross-referenced to file 800.20294/2. The second is a Justice Department communication enclosing a report on Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, although the information was believed actually to concern Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, Ltd.

people.name: Garrels
people.role: Official associated with Tokyo telegram no. 1225; position not stated

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers for File 894.65
subfiles.about: A filing sheet indexes two papers on Japanese factory secrecy legislation and Mitsubishi industrial interests.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a Tokyo telegram dated March 23, 1936, concerning a proposed Japanese law intended to prevent the divulgence of commercial information about Japanese factories; the entry directs readers to file 800.20294/2. It also lists a Justice Department paper dated May 20 that enclosed a report described as pertaining to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, while noting that the information was believed to refer instead to Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, Ltd. The printed notation “10/12/45” appears with the form number but may be a form date rather than the date on which the list was compiled.

interest: This filing aid is useful because it preserves concise descriptions of papers that are not reproduced in the surviving page and directs researchers to a separate decimal-file reference for the proposed secrecy law. It also records contemporary uncertainty over whether a Justice Department report concerned Mitsubishi Heavy Industries or Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, a distinction relevant to reconstructing American intelligence and administrative knowledge of Japanese corporate organization.
